newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rally to record close.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rally to record close.

text.p: French stocks reversed their early losses and rallied on Thursday to a second consecutive record close after shrugging off Wednesday's weakness on Wall Street.

"The bourse is ignoring bad news and has disconnected itself from Wall Street. It's trying to catch up relative to Frankfurt and London by finding new sources of inspiration in corporate results," a trader said.
The French market's blue-chip CAC-40 index rose 17.18 points, or 0.68 percent, to a closing record of 2,558.43 points, close to its all time intraday high of 2,558.60.
The CAC-40 February futures contract rose to 2,565 from 2,546.50 at Wednesday's close.
Volume was a heavy 8.9 billion francs.
Shares in Elf Aquitaine rose 1.04 percent to 584 francs, extending their gains on a positive report from Merrill Lynch.

Michelin shares rose 2.83 percent to 330.90 francs in brisk trading. Investors speculate a Goodyear-Sumitomo alliance will be to Bridgestone's detriment and to Michelin's advantage. They said Goodyear's good results were also bullish for Michelin.
Generale des Eaux and Havas, whose shares were suspended on Thursday, announced a restructuring of their media interests. Generale des Eaux will have 29.6 percent of Havas as a result.
